title: Yellowed Flaky Greek Semolina Custard Galaktoboureko
description: A traditional Greek dessert featuring semolina custard in a flaky phyllo crust, made with brown sugar and lardons-render for a unique flavor, and is diabetic-friendly due to the use of sugar substitutes.
instructions: Preheat the iron-teppan to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a medium saucepan, combine the semolina, brown sugar, and 2 cups of water, and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the lardons-render, eggs, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Allow the semolina mixture to cool to room temperature.
Unroll the phyllo dough and cut it into 4 equal pieces.
Place a piece of phyllo dough on the iron-teppan and brush it with melted butter.
Spoon the cooled semolina mixture onto the center of the phyllo dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the phyllo dough over the semolina mixture to form a triangle or rectangle shape, and brush the top with melted butter.
Repeat the process with the remaining phyllo dough and semolina mixture.
Bake the galaktoboureko for 35-40 minutes, or until the phyllo dough is golden brown.
Remove the galaktoboureko from the iron-teppan and allow it to cool for 10 minutes before serving.
